**Paperhue 0.4.0** adds **Natural colours**: photos keep their colours and brightness as closely as the
panel allows, instead of coming out pale. The previews now show the panel's own colours.

## New

### Natural colours (all apps)

A new **Colours** setting (「顏色」) sits next to **Grain**. It applies to photo pages, calendar backgrounds and
card photos.

- **Natural** (「自然」, the default) matches each colour to what the panel can really show:
  - photos are no longer too light;
  - blues, greens and skin tones keep their hue;
  - stray specks of an opposite colour are gone, such as orange dots in a lavender sky or green dots in a peach
    coat.
- **Classic** (「經典」) is the look of Paperhue 0.3, unchanged. Choose it if you prefer the lighter pictures, or
  for a picture already drawn in the seven pure colours, which it sends exactly as it is.
- **Grain** works with both. Changing to **Natural** sets **Grain** to **Standard**; you can change it afterwards.
  With Natural, **Soft**, **Softer** and **Smoothest** show bands of colour sooner than with Classic.
- The command line (`ulani`, `ulani-swift`) takes `--colours natural|classic`.

### Previews look like the device

- **Colours:** every preview (photos, calendar pages, notes and cards) now uses the panel's real, softer colours
  instead of bright screen colours. So previews look darker and less vivid than in 0.3, with Natural and Classic
  alike: that is how the device looks.
- **Small previews:** a preview smaller than the screen is averaged the way the eye mixes the panel's dots, so it
  no longer looks grainier than the device. This was most visible on the Mac.

## Upgrading from 0.3

- **Settings:** the first time 0.4.0 starts, **Colours** is **Natural** and **Grain** is **Standard**, whatever grain
  you had chosen. This also holds for the scheduled sync, even before you open the app. To get the old look back,
  choose **Classic** and your grain.
- **What is already on the device stays as it is until you send it again:**
  - photo pages and cards: push them again to get the new colours;
  - calendar pages with a background: they get the new colours at their next sync.
- **Mac:**
  - Replace Paperhue in Applications. Your pages and settings are kept.
  - macOS asks you to confirm the new download, as on the first install: on macOS 15 or newer, in
    **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway**.
  - Open Paperhue once after updating. macOS asks once for each calendar source whether Paperhue may use it: enter
    your Mac's password and choose **Always Allow**. If the daily schedule runs first, the question names
    "Paperhue" and the sync waits for your answer.
- **iPhone:** the web app updates itself. Reload it in Bluefy if it is still open.

## Download

- **Windows:** Paperhue.exe
- **Mac:** Paperhue-macOS.zip (macOS 14 or newer)
- **Android:** Paperhue-Android.apk
- **iPhone:** nothing to download. Open https://markhhm.github.io/ulani-epaper/ in the Bluefy browser.
